events.title: Comics of Care: Healing Through Graphic Medicine
events.venue: Sally T. WongAvery Library, 3100 Biomedical Sciences Wy La Jolla, CA 92093
events.description: What role can art and storytelling play in understanding health — and in healing? Explore comics, graphic novels and memoirs from UC San Diego Library's Graphic Medicine Collection: vividly drawn, personal stories about the experience of facing illness and finding care. In these pages, a single drawing can capture what's hard to put into words, sharing insights we can see and feel. We can learn from those who've faced health challenges and witness how they found their way through. Comics of Care is presented in connection with The Science of Story, a signature celebration of storytelling across UC San Diego. Returning for a third year during Comic-Con week, this series explores the art, craft and cultural power of narrative. In joining that conversation, this book exhibit shows how art and stories can help us heal — by letting us into another person's experience of illness and recovery. We hope these works deepen empathy for health struggles and spark discussion among patients, caregivers and clinicians who want to improve care. This collection was curated by UC San Diego librarians Jeffery Loo, Karen Heskett and Zemirah Ngow. Comics of Care is on view in the Sally T. WongAvery Library breezeway from June 29 to September 13, during the building's open hours.

events.title: Shark Summer at Birch Aquarium
events.description: Have you ever wondered what species swim in our local waters? Or wanted to know what makes sharks such unique animals? events.title: 25th Annual Paper Theatre Festival | Exhibition
events.venue: Geisel Library, 9701 Hopkins Drive, La Jolla, CA 92093
events.description: UC San Diego Library’s 25th anniversary season of Paper Theatre Festival returns this summer! Join us for a unique browsing opportunity at this year’s festival, which is taking the form of a colorful exhibition of paper theatres. Located on the 2nd (main) Floor of Geisel Library in The Nest, this display is free and open to the public. Explore at your leisure from July 14 through September 27, 2026, during the building's open hours. If you need assistance or would like an informal, pop-up performance in front of the exhibition on a prearranged date and time, contact exhibition curator Scott Paulson at spaulson@ucsd.edu. Additional Information Annual Paper Theatre Festival: It’s the Smallest Show on Earth! Paper theatre, also known as tabletop or toy theatre, dates back to Victorian-era London. Families would re-enact plays they saw in miniature by cutting and pasting souvenir poster kits purchased from local playhouses. These kits included scenery sheets, costumed paper dolls and condensed scripts. This vintage marketing tool and educational toy is making a comeback!UC San Diego Library plays a featured role in reviving this artful and educational hobby. On display are 25 seasons’ worth of miniature theatrical wonders, showcasing the enthusiastic work of our students, staff, alumni and community members.We are proud to host the oldest continually running paper theatre festival in the United States!An exhibition opening reception is scheduled for Tuesday, July 14, showcasing works from Scott Paulson '84, Rachel Almodovar, Elizabeth Hines, Carin Wallace, Anastasia Hunter, Christina Continelli, and visiting artist Nancy So Miller. Learn more about the exhibition opening reception.

events.title: Clarion Science Fiction and Fantasy Writer’s Masterclass
events.venue: The Loft, 3151 Matthews Ln, La Jolla, CA 92093
events.description: We’re thrilled to offer FREE registered admission for the Clarion Science Fiction and Fantasy Writer’s Masterclass at UC San Diego — an immersive, day-long experience exploring the craft and power of speculative fiction. Whether you’re a writer, reader, or simply curious about how science, imagination, and storytelling collide, this is a unique opportunity to learn from acclaimed authors and artists. In the Clarion Science Fiction and Fantasy Writer’s Masterclass events, attendees will have a chance to learn the fundamentals of speculative fiction from faculty and recent alumni of the selective Clarion Writers’ Workshop. Since 1968 Clarion has been the premier proving ground for writers of science, fiction, fantasy and horror, and now the public will have access to these instructors, their keen approaches to craft, their rich knowledge of the field, and their understanding of the traditions that have fed into the strong legacy Clarion has built over the years. Clarion instructors include: T.K. Rex (The Wildcraft Drones), Sumayyah Beck (Airrelle of the Maroon Witches) and Keynote Speaker Erin R. Roberts. Admission: FREE Includes: Breakfast and LunchMorning masterclass sessionLunch Keynote speakerAfternoon masterclass session

events.title: Summer with Stuart Concert Series
events.venue: Varies
events.description: Join us for the second annual Summer with Stuart, a pop-up concert series at various Stuart Collection Artworks. In partnership with local chamber musicians, we're presenting six weeks of free, family-friendly summer evening programming. Thursdays, 6 - 7 pm July 2: Sun God, Series kickoff with Westwind Brass As America marks its 250th birthday, Westwind Brass celebrates with Sousa-style marches, beloved folk and hymn tunes, jazz standards, Broadway showstoppers, and Hollywood film scores, all carried unamplified across Niki de Saint Phalle’s radiant Sun God lawn. The professional brass quintet — two trumpets, French horn, trombone, and tuba — sweeps across the American story, from the concert hall to the silver screen. Think Copland’s wide-open prairie sound and the brassy swagger of big-band jazz. Roughly 60–75 minutes of joyful noise for America’s 250th. Check out the band in advance: Listen to Westwind Brass Location: Sun God in Google Maps Parking: Scholars Parking Structure in Google Maps July 9: La Jolla Project, Left Coast Quintet As dusk settles over the Richard Fleischner’s La Jolla Project, five wind players gather among UC San Diego’s popular outdoor artwork, known as “Stonehenge,” for an evening that spans centuries in a single breath. The Left Coast Quintet — flute, oboe, clarinet, French horn, and bassoon — is one of music’s most eloquent ensembles: five distinct voices, one rich palette of color. Their program moves fluidly from Baroque counterpoint and Classical-era works (the woodwind quintet was born in Mozart’s day) to Romantic showpieces, contemporary discoveries, and imaginative arrangements of jazz and film music. What sets LCQ apart is its blend of warmth, humor, and polish — as at home with a Baroque partita as a film-score medley, and always ready to let the audience in on the fun. About 60 minutes where art, landscape, and music fold into one another. Check out the band in advance: Listen to Left Coast Quintet on their website Location: La Jolla Project in Google Maps Parking: Theater District Parking Structure in Google Maps July 16: Bear, Westwind Virtuosi Westwind Virtuosi returns to the most intimate setting in the series — the Bear courtyard, centered on Tim Hawkinson's massive granite boulder, Bear, also known as "Beryl." Something happens when strings play beside that stone: the granite seems to lean in and listen, holding the sound warm and close. This chamber ensemble — violin, viola, cello, and bass — draws on the heart of the string repertoire, from Haydn and Mozart through the Romantics, favoring lyrical slow movements that reward close listening: the cello’s deep warmth, the violin’s singing upper register, the feel of private conversation between musicians. Expect folk songs, tango, and lighter classics that translate beautifully to strings in the open air. Check out the band in advance: Listed to Westwind Virtuosi on their website Location: Bear in Google Maps Parking: Gilman Parking Structure in Google Maps July 23: Sun God, Manny Cepeda + Westwind Strings & Brass We’ve never done this before — and that’s exactly the point: For one electrifying hour, strings, brass, and the irresistible Manny Cepeda come together for a brand-new program of salsa, rhythm, and pure Latin joy. Sábor means flavor, and this concert has it in abundance. Cepeda — one of San Diego’s most beloved Latin musicians — leads a combined ensemble of Westwind string and brass players through salsa, cumbia, bolero, and cha-cha: forms rooted in Cuba, Colombia, and Puerto Rico and built on syncopated rhythm and call-and-response. The strings, unusual in a Latin dance band, lend lush warmth beneath the brass’s punch and swagger — the full sound of the great Tito Puente–era orchestras. The Sun God lawn's open footprint gives the music room to move. Check out the band in advance: Listen to Manny Cepeda on his website Location: Sun God in Google Maps Parking: Scholars Parking Structure in Google Maps July 30: La Jolla Project, Hornswoggle Thirty French horns gather at dusk at the La Jolla Project— and the results are elemental. Hornswoggle is one of the few ensembles in the country performing at this scale, and the French horn genuinely sounds better outdoors than in any hall. Thirty players spread across the grounds, dispersing the sound so it surrounds you rather than faces you — hunting calls and fanfares dating to the 17th and 18th centuries, hymn-like chorales and folk songs that bloom across horns in unison, and contemporary works written for the spatial possibilities of many horns in open air. Against the backdrop of La Jolla Project, it becomes a glorious, soaring wall of brass rolling into the sky. Check out the band in advance: Listen to Hornswoggle on their website Location: La Jolla Project in Google Maps Parking: Theater District Parking Structure in Google Maps August 6: Bear, Chamber Orchestra The Second Summer with Stuart ends the only way it could — with everyone on stage, Handel in the air, and Bear hearing Water Music for the very first time. Handel wrote Water Music in 1717 to be played outdoors, from a barge on the River Thames for King George I — one of the earliest masterpieces written for the open air. Three hundred years later, the combined forces of our summer series bring it back where it belongs: beside Tim Hawkinson’s granite boulder Bear, under a summer sky. Roughly twenty musicians — strings, brass, and winds drawn from every ensemble of the season, many of them former San Diego Chamber Orchestra players — gather for the full sweep of Handel’s suites: stately overtures, graceful minuets, and spirited hornpipes. Location: Bear in Google Maps Parking: Gilman Parking Structure in Google Maps Summer with Stuart Concert Series Sharable Flyer for Printing (Google Doc) Stuart Collection: The Stuart Collection at the University of California, San Diego – comprised of 22 permanent artworks by world-renowned artists, and growing – aims to question conventional understandings of public art in playful and insightful ways through our commissioning programs, and seeks to enrich the cultural, intellectual, and scholarly life of the UC San Diego campus and local San Diego community. We enhance public life through art that encourages thoughtful deliberation, an awareness of difference, mental and physical wellbeing, and that inspires creative solutions to complex issues; and continue to commission exciting new works from the world’s most important contemporary artists through our Landmarks, Emerging Artists and Public Programs.

events.description: Join MAVERiC Studio for the return of the Night Market, this year celebrating The Year of the Game Master in collaboration with the San Diego Table Top RPG Alliance. The 2026 showcase features the premiere of the studio’s first original cinematic short, “Dice Goblins.” This original short and companion mixed-reality experience was developed by MAVERiC Studio and Sony Group Corporation, inviting attendees to master the game with immersive technology. The evening also boasts a wide array of industry guests, panels, shows and activations all night long. The Alumni Arcade returns with all new experiences and for the first time ever, a community-led “Tavern of Tables,” which will transform UC San Diego Park & Market into a massive table top and immersive gaming hub. Celebrate the studio’s third anniversary, as the STUDiO Players return to Park & Market’s Guggenheim Theater and close the evening with the studio’s signature series, the Dragon City Chronicles actual play. Don’t just watch the game, master it. Get your FREE tickets or buy a VIP ticket to support the MAVERiC Studio Night Market this summer and follow us all year long as we celebrate The Year of the Game Master at the MAVERiC Studio Night Market! Comic Con Badges are NOT required. FREE GENERAL ADMISSION The MAVERiC Studio Night Market exhibition is FREE to attend. The studio’s artists and content creators have an arcade token system, purchasable onsite, day of, or by the UC San Diego Bookstore in advance. VIP PUB PASS Support the show now for $75.00 and gain access to the whole show! You’ll have a priority seat for our Feature Presentations in the Guggenheim Black Box theater, AND our game master experiences in the Tavern of Tables! You’ll even get free play in our Alumni Arcade all night! Ripped from the pages of the Tavern of Tables, DJ Filth Wizard takes the transdimensional stage and transforms the Gugenhime into a Night Ending dance floor! _______________________________ FEATURED SAN DIEGO COMMUNITY PARTNERS: About Tavern Tales: Tavern Tales Events is a San Diego-based company that provides public programming for the Tabletop Roleplaying community in Southern California. All of our events focus on inclusivity, connection, and accessibility for new players and veterans alike. Attending a Tavern Tales event is just the start as each provides a further introduction to many local gaming organizations and businesses already in existence. We do a number of events ranging from our flagship Find Your Party series, Learn-to-Play opportunities, and custom Non-Profit programming. Discover Tavern Tales. About LDDSD: Ladies of D&D San Diego is a welcoming, femme‑centered TTRPG community creating safe, inclusive spaces for players to learn, connect, and tell stories together. Through supportive tables, workshops, and an active Discord hub, the group empowers new and experienced adventurers to build confidence, friendships, and joyful collaborative play. Learn more about the Ladies of D&D San Diego. About The San Diego Tabletop Alliance: The San Diego Tabletop Alliance connects the region’s tabletop gaming communities, creators, stores, and events through a unified discovery hub. By aggregating local groups, actual‑play shows, meetups, and resources, the Alliance strengthens San Diego’s tabletop ecosystem and makes it easier for players to find their community. Discoer the San Diego Tabletop Alliance. FEATURED PARTNERS: About the Science of Story Back for a third year, The Science of Story returns to UC San Diego as a signature experience. Hosted with partners across UC San Diego, this immersive six-day event series explores the art, craft, and cultural power of storytelling from speculative fiction to science communication, graphic novels to groundbreaking social commentary. The Science of Story invites writers, readers, fans, and thinkers to come together and dive into the many dimensions of narrative. Learn more about the Science of Story Experience - ArtPower About the UC San Diego Office of Innovation and Commercialization The Office of Innovation and Commercialization (OIC) accelerates the commercialization of research discoveries created by UC San Diego faculty, staff, students, and alumni. OIC offers patent and copyright support, market assessments, business development services, and mentorship through campus‑wide entrepreneurship programs such as the IDEAS Council, the Institute for the Global Entrepreneur, and the StartBlue Ocean Enterprise Accelerator. Learn more about the Office of Innovation & Commercialization About Sony XYN™: XYN™ (/zin/) is an integrated software and hardware solution that supports the creation of spatial content. By using Sony’s unique technology, it accurately captures the real world and combines the content with a wide range of third-party tools to enable flexible workflow construction. Learn more about Sony XYN™. Watch another immersive experience by MAVERiC Studio using Sony’s XYN solutions (mocopi and Spatial Reality Display). About the Technology Strategy Committee of Sony Group Corporation The Technology Strategy Committee is a technology based activity body across the Sony Group. It strengthens the Group's technological capabilities to support Sony's future leap forward through cross-organizational exchanges, and serves as a forum for sharing the most advanced technology information and enhancing technological capabilities across business units. It also focuses on the development of the early career engineers, supporting their growth and journey toward achieving their goals. About MAVERIC Studio: The Mixed Augmented Virtual Extended Reality Innovation Center Studio is UC San Diego’s production-based studio for immersive storytelling and innovation and a public-private training ground where students and alumni earn real-world credit by designing stories, worlds, and experiences that blend physical and digital reality. This is not a lab. It’s a working studio. We offer a diverse range of opportunities designed to empower seekers with essential XR skills. events.venue: Solana Ranch Park, San Diego, CA, 13605 Pacific Highlands Ranch Pkwy, San Diego, CA
events.description: We will enjoy a neighborhood park and surrounding dirt trails near the Pacific Highlands Ranch area in Carmel Valley. Fairly easy, mostly flat walk on dirt trail and sidewalk. Afterwards we will take a quick lap around the recently renovated shopping center for some distraction training opportunities. Total distance is under 2 miles, just about an hour. Meet at the grassy area at the front of Solana Ranch park, just off Pacific Highlands Ranch Pkwy. **Welcome to Real Dog Box Community Pack Walks!** We welcome **ALL** dogs, breeds, and temperaments. Enjoying our pack walks? Support our Host & Sponsor: Real Dog Box This local small business delivers air dried treats and chews to your doorstep. Get a free bag of treats when you order your 1st box: real.dog/takkopakko or shop with us for treats and chews in person after the walk! We have grown an amazing and supportive community. To keep everyone safe and promote a calm environment, by attending our walks you are expected to follow & respect our rules: 1. All dogs must remain on leash at all times, handlers must maintain a 3 foot lead. NO retractable or bungee leashes permitted. 1. NO greeting dogs inside or outside our pack until the walk is over, with permission. Please always keep dogs on leash. We know some dogs are friends, but use this time to practice following structured socialization. 1. Maintain at least a 6 foot distance to prevent nose-to-nose/tail interactions. If your dog is a beginner or reactive, we recommend taking more space if needed, by walking at the back of the pack. 1. Come prepared and advocate for your dog. Bring adequate water, poop bags, treats, etc. Monitor your dog and always do what’s best for them. If your dog is slowing down, consider stopping early. If your dog is panting, request a break to give them some water. Our Community Pack Leaders will be leading the walk and can answer any questions that come up. We are looking forward to meeting you and your pup!

events.venue: Duane J. Roth Auditorium at Sanford Consortium for Regenerative Medicine, 2880 Torrey Pines Scenic Drive, La Jolla, California - 92037
events.description: In welcoming U.S. President Donald Trump to Beijing in May for a summit, Chinese President Xi Jinping sought to find an answer to the question of whether China and the U.S. would be able to overcome the Thucydides Trap and create a new paradigm of major country relations. After two days of intense conversation, the two leaders offered a tentative “yes,” proposing to create a new era of what they called “constructive strategic stability.” Following in the tradition of Susan Shirk, who insists on asking difficult questions and challenging conventional wisdom, the political scientist Graham Allison will devote this lecture to examining both the promise and the limits of that vision. 4:15 - 5:00 PM — Reception on the Terrace5:00 - 6:30 PM — Public Lecture in Roth Auditorium Presider: Meghan O’Sullivan, Director, The Belfer Center; Jeane Kirkpatrick Professor of the Practice of International Affairs, Harvard Kennedy School Speaker: Graham Allison, Douglas Dillon Professor of Government, Harvard Kennedy School ___________________________________ This public lecture is organized by the 21st Century China Center (21CCC) at the UC San Diego School of Global Policy and Strategy.
